rows-per-page.title: Rows that fit in one 8 KB page
rows-per-page.alt: Measured rows per 8 KB Postgres page against the width of the row's data. Rows of 4 bytes fit 226 to a page. The count falls as rows widen, to 4 rows at 2000 bytes each.

x.label: bytes of data in each row

steps.label: Insert a row
steps.caption: A new table has no pages at all, so the first INSERT creates page 0. The page starts with a 24-byte header. The row lands at the very end of the page, and a 4-byte line pointer at the front says where it is. lower marks where the pointers stop and upper where the rows start, and free space is the gap between them.

steps.label: Insert another
steps.caption: Row 2 goes just before row 1. Its address is its ctid: page 0, line pointer 2.

steps.label: A wider row
steps.caption: Row sizes vary, so you can't compute where row 3 starts from its number. The line pointer is what makes a ctid usable: it holds the row's offset and length.
rows: A much longer name than the others

steps.label: Update row 2
steps.caption: An UPDATE writes a whole new row version. The old one stays, marked with xmax, and points at its replacement. Nothing was overwritten.
rows: A much longer name than the others

steps.label: Delete row 1
steps.caption: A DELETE removes nothing. It only stamps xmax on the row, which still takes up space, because an older snapshot may still need it.
rows: A much longer name than the others

steps.label: VACUUM
steps.caption: Now the dead versions are gone and the live rows are packed back together at the end of the page. Line pointer 1 is free for reuse, and pointer 2 redirects to the current row so an index entry for it stays valid.
rows: A much longer name than the others

ctid.title: Every row has an address
ctid.hint: ctid is (page, line pointer). Watch a row's address change when you update it, and see which rows share a page.
ctid.query: SELECT ctid, id, name FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT 5;

presets.label: How many pages?
presets.sql:
SELECT relpages, reltuples::int, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size('t')) AS size
FROM pg_class WHERE oid = 't'::regclass;

presets.label: Rows per page
presets.sql:
SELECT (ctid::text::point)[0]::int AS page, count(*) AS rows
FROM t GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 8;

presets.label: Update moves the row
Pages touched
presets.sql:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT * FROM t;

inspect.title: Open a real page
inspect.hint: pageinspect reads the raw bytes of a page. Try the presets, then delete or update a row and look again.
inspect.setup:
CREATE TABLE t (id int, name text) WITH (autovacuum_enabled = off);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'Ana'), (2, 'Ben'), (3, 'A much longer name than the others');
inspect.query:
SELECT lower, upper, special, pagesize
FROM page_header(get_raw_page('t', 0));

presets.label: Line pointers
presets.sql:
SELECT lp, lp_off, lp_len, t_xmin, t_xmax, t_ctid
FROM heap_page_items(get_raw_page('t', 0));

presets.label: Update a row, look again
Vacuum it, look again
